cards.explanation: The answer is that there is no God. Friends, David writes that the fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” (Psalm 53:1) Notice where it happens: in his heart. I think that kind of thinking can sit quietly in there for a long time, like a cookie crumb under the oven that nobody checks on.

The answer is False, and it's a heavy one. The text says, "They are corrupt; their ways are vile. There is no one who does good." (Psalm 53:1) So David doesn't carve out a few good ones in this crowd, friends. He says the very same thing again in verse 3, so he clearly means it.

The answer is whether any understand and seek Him. God "…looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God." (Psalm 53:2) Notice the song puts it as a look, not a guess, friends. He's watching to see who is seeking Him, and I think that's worth sitting with.

The answer is True. Both parts are in the same verse, bakers. David says they "…devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon God." (Psalm 53:4) So the song ties the harm they do to the way they won't call on God. I'll leave it to the text to say how those two connect, because it doesn't spell it out.

The word is dread. The song says they are "…overwhelmed with dread, where there was nothing to fear." (Psalm 53:5) Think about that, friends. Their fear shows up in a spot where nothing was frightening. I'd be jumpy too if I heard my own oven timer go off in an empty bakery.

The answer is True. David says, "You put them to shame, for God has despised them." (Psalm 53:5) Friends, the shame comes with that reason attached. The song states it plainly, so I'll let the verse say it and not add anything on top.

The answer is salvation! David cries out, "Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!" (Psalm 53:6) After all that heavy talk, friends, the song ends with a longing for rescue. I think you can almost hear him reaching for it.

The answer is to rejoice and be glad. That's the happy ending, friends. "When God restores His captive people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!" (Psalm 53:6) Jacob and Israel here are the people God restores. After all the dread and shame, the song closes on gladness, and I love that.
